summary.name: Rubber Hose Animation. The label is normalized from a Cuphead-inspired reference, not an explicitly named source style.
summary.visualIdentity: Vintage rubber-hose cartoon style with rounded figures, flexible tube-like limbs, bold silhouettes, and expressive poses. Characters keep a stable identity while anticipation, arcs, rhythmic poses, and clear reactions carry the action. Arbitrary limb deformation and identical bounces on every object are to be avoided.
summary.suitableUses: Explicitly suited to illustrated mascots and characters, character gags, and cartoon or rigged character scenes. Also listed as a good fit for product or explainer scenes that already include an expressive character. Looping or music-timed uses are inferred from the suggested pairing with a rhythm-based style.
summary.limitations: Requires readable character silhouettes and a stable identity across scenes. Limb motion must stay within deliberate arcs and pivots, not unconstrained distortion. Color is limited to monochrome with no added accent hues. Simulated appearance is not evidence of physical production, and stateful simulations must be cached. Frame rate, duration, and aspect ratio are unspecified.
summary.palette: Suggested two-token monochrome: background #F4ECD9 (warm off-white) and foreground #1C1B18 (near-black ink). These are authored suggestions, and task or approved brand colors override them. Gradients are disabled. Apparent tone should come from hatching, screen patterns, or opacity rather than extra hues. The pair has a 14.636:1 contrast ratio, but composited frames must still be checked.
summary.motionAndInteraction: Motion should use deliberate arcs, pivots, squash-and-stretch, and rhythmic poses with anticipation before key actions. Sharp cuts, impacts, and reading holds may be preserved rather than eased. Video motion is driven from composition time. No live interaction is specified for this style. Motion references 006, 012, and 015 are optional and must be screened against the scene.
summary.audio: The source does not specify audio for this style and gives only suggestion dimensions. Options include background music, voiceover, sound effects, ambience, or silence, chosen by topic and audience. Music-timed use is suggested with a rhythm-based companion style. Any explicit user audio requirement takes priority, and speech must remain intelligible.
summary.assetRequirements: Character artwork should be built from curved paths and replaceable poses, or supplied as baked frame sequences. Fonts and assets must be loaded before rendering. Canvas 2D and SVG handle drawing, and PixiJS can composite large sets of sprites. Motion reference 006 requires facial layers or a rig. No source asset files or audio assets are supplied.
summary.combinations: Suggested pairing with style-105 provides beat-keyed timing, with different rhythmic patterns per character and no identical bounce on every element. Suggested pairing with style-052 provides letterpress intertitle cards using the same black-on-cream palette and a fixed grid. Avoid colored inks, letterpress texture on characters, and audio that comprehension depends on.
summary.productionApproach: HyperFrames is the default for scene assembly, timing, audio sync, validation, and export, with Remotion used only under its documented fallback conditions. Canvas 2D and SVG own the visual construction, with PixiJS optional. Each animated property should have one motion owner, such as GSAP or Motion. Verify opening, action, transition, and closing frames, plus loop seams, before delivery.
